meta.title: The Hidden Cost Every Trader Pays That Never Shows Up As A Fee
meta.hook: You can buy and sell a stock and lose money instantly, with zero fees.
meta.description: Every stock has two prices at once: the bid, what buyers will pay, and the ask, what sellers want. That gap is the spread. Buy at the ask and sell at the bid a second later, and you lose the spread even if the price never moved. On heavily traded stocks it's tiny; on thinly traded ones it can quietly cost far more than a broker's commission. Educational content only, not financial advice.

scenes.narration: You can buy a stock, sell it one second later, and lose money. With zero fees charged.

scenes.narration: That small gap between them is called the spread. And it's not a fee. It's built into the price itself.

scenes.narration: Buy at the ask, then sell at the bid a moment later, and you lose that gap. Even if the stock price never moved.

scenes.narration: On a heavily traded stock, that gap is tiny, often a penny or less. On a thinly traded one, it can be much wider.

scenes.narration: It never shows up as a line item. But every trade quietly pays it. Follow for more.
